Question: Is “financial point of view” the sole consideration when determining whether an offer is superior?

Merger Agreement: Section 8.7 – Offer Evaluation and Decision Protocol. 
(a) Prior to any recommendation change or termination under this Agreement, the Company Board shall conduct a comprehensive review of any Acquisition Proposal. This review shall include, inter alia, an assessment of quantitative financial metrics, prevailing market conditions, strategic alignment with the Company’s long-term objectives, regulatory implications, and expected operational synergies. 
(b) In making its determination, the Board is mandated to consult with its financial advisors, legal counsel, and industry experts. While quantitative financial analysis is required, it is expressly integrated with qualitative assessments such as strategic benefit evaluation and compliance with relevant laws and industry standards. 
(c) Notwithstanding any favorable financial figures, an offer will only be deemed ‘Superior’ if it concurrently meets all of the following conditions: (i) demonstrates robust regulatory compliance; (ii) presents clear strategic advantages beyond mere monetary gain; and (iii) promises operational improvements that align with or exceed industry benchmarks. 
(d) Should the evaluation occur solely on the basis of financial metrics without due consideration of the aforementioned strategic, regulatory, and operational factors, the Board shall not classify the offer as Superior, regardless of the financial attractiveness. 
(e) The Company is required to provide a detailed notice to the Parent company that outlines the multiple criteria—both financial and non-financial—that were considered in reaching its determination regarding the superiority of any Acquisition Proposal.
